editorial:
The Stolen Jools is a 1931 charity short released through Paramount on April 4, 1931. Per Wikipedia, it was distributed to raise funds for the National Vaudeville Artists Tuberculosis Sanitarium. The plot is a small whodunit: Norma Shearer's jewels vanish at the Screen Stars Annual Ball, and child performer Mitzi Green, who witnessed the robbery, solves the case. Its value to a creator is the cast. Wallace Beery, Buster Keaton, Edward G. Robinson, Joan Crawford, Fay Wray, Gary Cooper, and Laurel and Hardy all appear. Few other films gather so many 1931 Hollywood faces in one reel.

The rights trap is the music. Wikipedia reports that when Blackhawk Films reprinted the short, the Harry Fox Agency would not license sync rights unless the film itself was shown to be licensed. Blackhawk deleted the song snippets, and a Thunderbird Films print kept them. As a 1931 film, its print is not free by term alone. A 1931 work's renewal window is 1958 or 1959. I have not searched the renewal sections of those volumes in full or the Copyright Office catalog, so the print's status is unconfirmed. Check the renewal records yourself before relying on it. The songs have not been identified or checked as separate works, so clear or cut them separately.
faq: Is The Stolen Jools in the public domain?

Not confirmed. It is a 1931 film, so it depends on whether the copyright was renewed in 1958 or 1959. I have not searched the renewal sections of those volumes in full, and I have not searched the Copyright Office catalog. Use the links above to check before you reuse it.
Can I use the song snippets in the film?

Treat them as a separate clearance risk. Their copyright status has not been checked. Per Wikipedia, Blackhawk Films cut them from its reprint after the Harry Fox Agency would not license sync rights. Use a print without the songs, or clear them.
